brief: Daily color from GS's Privorotsky. US tech rebound carried into Asia (Hynix, Samsung, KOSPI higher). The open question is whether this is an oversold Nasdaq bounce or something more durable, helped by risk premium already priced ahead of next week's political events, so the market struggles to go down. In the Gulf, Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani mediation in Tehran has produced nothing substantive. Odds of a breakthrough are low, oil has eased off Friday's highs, but no progress by Thursday could restart the escalatory ladder into the weekend. HSBC fell 5.6% in Hong Kong as UK and Hong Kong deposit competition compresses bank NII, a risk GS flags spreading across Europe. In AI, neoclouds fell on Musk's financing and consolidation comments, but credit spreads eased off Friday's wides, the most important signal to watch, since a rising cost of capital is reshaping the sector's economics even as demand stays robust (Celestica, Cadence, Rambus all beat). The debate is discounting future cash flows, not demand. Stable front-end rates help risk, and credit easing would be the bigger catalyst. Hyperscaler earnings plus the Fed are this week's focus, judged on capex, backlog conversion, free cash flow and financing mix.
